name: Cotoname
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Texas coahuiltecan-area isolate known only from short wordlists; no phonological description located

sources.citation: Gatschet, Albert S. 1887. Ethnologic results obtained upon an expedition in the south-west of the United States. Science 9(221): 411-413.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 412, of COMECRUDO: "There is also a tendency to oxytonize many words, especially substantives, although the accent shifts, as in other Indian languages." Next sentence: "The same simplicity and paucity of sounds is found in the Cotoname language, formerly spoken in the same district." The accent remark is about Comecrudo; only the sound-inventory remark is extended to Cotoname.

sources.citation: Haukur Þorgeirsson & Alaric Hall. 2024. The Cotoname language - the primary sources. Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.13368224. 39 pp. (facsimile edition of Berlandier BL Add. MS 38720 and Gatschet NAA MS 297-a/b with alphabetized vocabulary)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; introduction covers sources and orthography only (Gatschet used early Americanist notation; Berlandier French-based spelling). Defers all analysis to Þorgeirsson, 'The Cotoname language - an analysis', IJAL.

sources.citation: Swanton, John R. 1940. Linguistic material from the tribes of southern Texas and northeastern Mexico. Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 127. Washington: GPO. (Cotoname-English vocabulary of Gatschet 1886, pp. 118-121; phonetics pp. 8-10)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only p. 10: "The accents in Comecrudo, Cotoname, and the Karankawa recorded by Dr. Gatschet are as given by the last named investigator." The vocabulary prints Gatschet's accent marks (kata'm, garo'pa, ka'pra..) but states no rule.

sources.citation: Swanton, John R. 1915. Linguistic position of the tribes of southern Texas and northeastern Mexico. American Anthropologist n.s. 17: 17-40.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on word accent; pp. 20-21 only general remarks that Karankawa, Comecrudo, Cotoname etc. are 'vocalic' with some final consonants.
